Beanstalk governance takeover with flash loaned voting power [cite:rkt-0004::0]. Voting weight must be read through the ERC20Votes getPastVotes accessor at a snapshot block chosen before the proposal was visible, and the execution delay must exceed the window in which the snapshot can be gamed [cite:c4r-0013::0]. An attacker can flash borrow the governance token, vote with the borrowed weight, and repay in the same transaction at no cost [cite:c4r-0013::0]. The attacker submitted a proposal, waited for the emergency commit window to mature, then flash borrowed roughly one billion dollars of liquidity from Aave and Uniswap, deposited it for stalk, passed their own proposal with a supermajority, and executed a payload that transferred the protocol treasury to themselves, all inside one transaction and one block [cite:rkt-0004::0].

Liquidation can be blocked by a reverting receive function. liquidate pushes the seized collateral to the liquidator with a raw call and reverts if the call fails [cite:c4r-0015::0]. A borrower who is also the counterparty of the liquidator, or a smart contract borrower with a reverting receive, can make every liquidation attempt revert and keep an underwater position open until the protocol accrues bad debt [cite:c4r-0015::0]. Because the bonus is a flat amount rather than a fraction of the seized collateral, the strategy is profitable for dust positions and drains the fund without any bad debt being cleared [cite:shk-0002::0]. Arithmetic that wraps because it is performed in an unchecked block, in Solidity below 0.8, or through an unsafe cast to a narrower type [cite:tax-SWC-101::0]. Because the soft liquidation discount scales with how unhealthy a position is, the discount on a position made arbitrarily unhealthy in a single transaction was large enough to extract far more collateral than the debt cleared [cite:rkt-0003::0].
